Plan Quality Management | Practice of defining the project’s quality objectives and expectations, and planning the tasks, procedures, tools, and participants that will perform the quality activities for the project. We plan the strategy, processes, and tools used to perform the three components of the project’s overall quality program: quality assurance, quality control, and quality support.
Execute Quality Assurance | Practices to establish and manage project delivery standards, monitor adherence, and make process improvements. We verify that the project has the processes and tools it needs to deliver a high-quality solution and that the project team is using them effectively. These objectives are accomplished by performing the following tasks: managing the project methods and templates, managing the project standards and guidelines, and performing the quality assessment activities planned for the project.
Monitor and Control Quality | Practices that monitor project results and identify corrective, preventative, and improvement actions. We perform the deliverable reviews planned for the project, complete the deliverable sign-offs planned for the project, and manage the detailed project metrics plan for the project.
Execute Quality Support | Practices whereby non-project specialists are leveraged to assess, advise, and assist the project team, providing additional oversight and support to the project. We execute the quality support activities planned for the project, as defined in the quality management plan.

Development & Integration Methodology

Type | Description
Standard SAP Integration Content | Leverage SAP’s native, out-of-the-box integration content wherever possible. This includes pre-delivered content for SuccessFactors, Service cloud and several other solutions. Benefits: Standard content accelerates implementation, ensures compatibility with SAP’s roadmap, and reduces maintenance overhead.
Application Programming Interface (API) | Prioritize the use of standard, whitelisted APIs published in the SAP API Hub for all integration requirements. Where necessary, extend these APIs using SAP’s “clean core” principles, leveraging both in-app and side-by-side extensibility options. In direct migration scenarios, we will try to reuse existing ABAP proxy code after code remediation.
SAP Events | Where real-time, event-driven integration is required, leverage SAP’s standard event framework (or leverage ASAPIO add-on for custom events) to enable asynchronous event-driven communication. This approach supports scalable, decoupled architectures and enhances responsiveness across business processes.
IDOCs | IDocs remain a preferred approach for certain scenarios, such as EDI integrations. SAP S/4HANA also provides a robust, out-of-the-box framework for IDoc monitoring and reprocessing. Best Practice: We recommend using only future-ready, cloud-compatible IDocs and avoiding complex customizations. This ensures alignment with SAP’s strategic direction and simplifies ongoing support.
File based integration | File-based integration should be reserved and approved for exception cases, such as when standard SAP programs require or generate specific file formats (for e.g. XML and BAI formats for banks) when handling confidential files with sensitive PII data, or for high-volume, full-load data exchanges between on-premise systems. These integrations should follow an asynchronous pattern, and comprehensive stress and performance testing must be conducted. Our team has extensive experience designing such solutions, often combining file-based methods with an API-first approach to maintain a clean core.
